findings.text: s67's done-when has two clauses that cannot both be the node's measure: `test_every_staged_write_reaches_the_owner` passes at the head, and a writer classified as a bypass leaves the test red naming that writer. The assertion at tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py:42 is an equality between the whole observed set and the expected set, so "not adding a bypass" is not a distinct behaviour the test can be made to express — the failure is an undifferentiated set diff, and the section names no mechanism by which the test would "name that writer" as a bypass rather than as an extra entry. A worker that met a bypass would have to invent that mechanism, and its promotion would rest on a red gate.

findings.reason: a section that names a recurring cause and ships only its symptom leaves the plan scheduling the fourth recurrence; the author would either add a mechanism that puts the census in the gate of a node touching a writer, or state explicitly that recurrence is accepted and why.
findings.text: s67 attributes the recurrence to a systemic cause in its own Why ("a node that adds a staged writer runs only the tests that cover its own write paths, so it never runs this census, and main turns red at the next node that does"), then prescribes only the addition of four expected-set entries. Nothing in "What changes" alters that cause, so by the section's own account the next node to add a staged writer turns main red a fourth time, and this node's deliverable is a one-round patch rather than a repair. I reproduced the defect at base cd2ccf0acd: the test fails with exactly the four named extras, which confirms the symptom and says nothing about why the census is unreachable from a node's gate.
